rationale: Continuing the authorized source work on the deferred transport surface: closing the remaining concurrency questions I had listed (whether a pooled connection can be handed to two callers, the consumer back-pressure policy) and reading the in-process transport's delivery contract that the captured tests rest on. Reading only; no defect asserted, no obligation created.

feedback.answered: Three previously open transport questions are answered by reading. First, a pooled connection is exclusive: getPooledConn takes connPoolLock, pops the last entry of the per-target slice, nils the slot and truncates the slice before returning (net_transport.go 366-378), so one connection cannot be handed to two callers concurrently, and returnConn only re-pools below maxPool (434-446). Second, the NetworkTransport's consumer channel is created unbuffered - `consumeCh: make(chan RPC)` in the constructor (211-231) - so each inbound connection's handler blocks on its dispatch send until the Raft main loop receives, which serialises inbound RPC handling and makes head-of-line blocking the normal condition that the heartbeat fast path exists to shortcut; the main loop reads exactly that channel (raft.go runFollower/runCandidate/leaderLoop via trans.Consumer). Third, the in-process transport used by the captured tests delivers by pushing an RPC with a one-buffered response channel onto the peer's consumer channel under a send timeout and then waits under a separate response timeout (inmem_transport.go 176-199, reached from every typed RPC method at 101-174), and the two failures are distinguished in the error text ('send timed out' versus 'command timed out'); a send timeout therefore means not delivered, while a command timeout can return an error to the caller even though the peer already accepted and may still process the request.
